title: OpenAI raises GPT-6.1 Sol default context length to 500,000 tokens
key_facts: GPT-6.1 Sol now starts with a 500,000-token context length in Codex and ChatGPT Work, up from 272,000 tokens; the change landed on 11 Oct 2026.
That is an extra 228,000 tokens of room by default; the default is only a starting point and users can override it.
GPT-6.1 Sol supports a maximum context window of 1,050,000 tokens: up to 922,000 for input and up to 128,000 for output.
OpenAI eliminated long-context surcharges for subscription users of GPT-6.1 Sol.
The published API rates are $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, in line with the predecessor's.
OpenAI framed the change as a response to user feedback, to make the model better at long contexts and multi-step tasks.

GPT-6.1 Sol launched on 29 Sep 2026 at OpenAI's DevDay; it is pitched at complex coding, heavy computer use and professional work, with performance described as closely aligned with the flagship GPT-6 Astra at a much lower running cost.
It is available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users, and through the API.
